transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-13 16:00 PDT | Duration: 58m | Recording id: ff-20260513-axiom-cache-batch-01
Attendees (Redwood): Jordan Kline (AE), Samir Patel (SE), Ana Ruiz (Product)
Attendees (Axiom Health): Dr. Priya Rao (Head of ML), Marcus Li (Platform Eng), Leah Ortiz (Compliance), Tim Wu (SRE)
Shared artifacts: savings spreadsheet (drive/axiom-savings-may2026.xlsx), demo notebook (github/redwood/axiom-demo)

Summary: quick Optimize console walkthrough focused on batching and prefix/KV cache tradeoffs for Axiom's clinical assistant workload. Goal: show likely 30-55% per-token cost savings with session-prefetch + modest batching while keeping 95th pct latency under 300ms for interactive flows.
Topics covered: workload profile, prefix/KV prefetch heuristics, batch sizing, TTL and sessionization, failover to small model variants, dedicated vs hosted latency tradeoffs, compliance notes (data retention, KMS).

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick agenda — walk through Optimize recommendations, show console sims, then Q&A.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks, we basically want to understand where batching helps vs when prefetching prefix/KV is the right move. Our users are clinicians doing short dialogs — mostly 30-150 token responses, lots of repeated patient context across session.
[00:32] Samir: got it, so this is a high session-affinity workload which is good for prefix/KV. A quick question about token sizes — do you have distribution?
[00:45] Marcus: yeah i uploaded a sample earlier, mean response 95 tokens, median 72, tail to 300 on long summarizations. Request rate is spiky — 1.2k RPS peak across region, steady 250 RPS baseline.
[01:12] Jordan: perfect. we'll run two scenarios in the console — interactive clinician flow (low latency target 200-300ms) and batch summarization jobs (throughput oriented).
[01:30] Samir: opening the Optimize console — first recommendation: enable prefix cache for sessionized flows with a 12h TTL for patient sessions, reason being clinicians come back within the shift. This gives high hit rates for the first few tokens and shrinks compute by ~30% for typical prompts.
[02:05] Priya: what's the risk of stale context if TTL is long? we have privacy retention needs.
[02:12] Ana: good call — TTL is orthogonal to persistence retention. TTL here is a short-lived in-memory prefix/KV cache; persistence for audit is still controlled via your retention policy and KMS. We suggest TTL <= 24h for clinical use, default 12h.
[02:35] Tim: Leah, anything from compliance?
[02:37] Leah: need to confirm KMS integration and audit logs, also network egress for hosted mode is a question — will need SOC2 docs.
[02:45] Jordan: we'll add SOC2 and network diagrams to the follow-up package.
[03:01] Samir: switching to batch sizing: for the interactive flow we recommend a small micro-batch of 4-8 with a hard latency cap. Why? because continuous batching reduces per-token cost, but at high concurrency you hit memory/KV contention, so we balance by limiting concurrent inference kernels and applying adaptive batching.
[03:28] Samir: demo sim: baseline (no cache, single request) cost estimate ~0.020 $/k token, with prefix cache hit 40% and batch size 6 average we show 38% cost reduction to ~0.012 $/k token. this is a simplified example — console shows per-route token breakdown and token/time charts.
[04:05] Marcus: those numbers are big for us, are those for *hosted* or *dedicated*?
[04:10] Samir: this is hosted mixed variants. Dedicated will push cost lower per token but you trade commit and operational overhead. For Axiom given your spiky peaks, we recommend hosted with Dedicated-reserve for baseline plus burst to hosted for peaks — Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback.
[04:36] Priya: how do you model fallback? if dedicated is saturated, do requests go to a smaller model or to hosted same model?
[04:45] Samir: routes are configurable: policy can route to same model on hosted, a quantized variant, or a family fallback (smaller model) depending on latency and quality SLOs. Console sim showed a canary rule where 10% of traffic used a quantized variant during saturations.
[05:12] Jordan: note on quality monitoring — Optimize can link regressions to prompt sets; if fallback causes weird outputs we flag immediate rollback.
[05:29] Priya: ok good. show us the sessionization numbers.
[05:35] Samir: slide: sessionization + prefetch — if you prefetch KV for predicted next-turn tokens with lookahead of 8 tokens, you get a ~12ms median latency drop on the tail; combined with batching it's cumulative. For our sample, prefetch hit rate projected 52% for clinician workflows.
[06:02] Tim: where does prefetch live? does it send extra tokens and cost more?
[06:07] Samir: prefetch requests are cheap — they are warmup/k-v cache population calls that aren't full generation, typically fast and smaller. Optimize models the tradeoff: prefetch cost vs saved generation cost. For many dialog flows, prefetch pays back quickly because generation is expensive per token.
[06:35] Priya: what about long docs (patient notes) where the prefix is big — does KV grow unbounded?
[06:42] Samir: we use bounded KV with LRU + TTL. console lets you tune prefix truncation and chunking. For long docs we recommend on-demand chunking + embedding-indexed lookup to reduce KV size.
[07:05] Marcus: can you show me the console live sim with our numbers?
[07:10] Samir: switching to the scenario builder — uploading the sample workload (Jordan confirms sample). Simulator shows three lanes: baseline, prefix-only, prefix+batch. you can toggle peak RPS and request distribution.
[07:38] [08:00] Samir: here are 3 quick outputs: baseline 100% generation = monthly cost estimate $9.4k; prefix-only reduces to $6.2k (~34%); prefix+batch reduces to $4.9k (~48%). of course these assume the hit rates and batch sizes in the sample.
[08:26] Leah: are audits maintained if we use prefix cache? we need traceability per request.
[08:31] Samir: yes every request has headers and audit logs; prefix cache entries are logged with keys redacted per KMS policy. We'll include the log retention options and sample log entries in the follow-up.
[08:58] Priya: question about latency SLO at 95th percentile — can batching push us over the 300ms?
[09:06] Samir: good point — adaptive batching respects latency budgets. you set a target (ex: 95th <= 300ms), optimizer constrains batch windows and will flush early for critical requests, while throughput jobs can wait for larger batch windows.
[09:26] Jordan: also note you can prioritize traffic classes — clinician UI requests get priority over background summarization.
[09:36] Tim: SRE question: how much KV memory per session? we need to capacity plan.
[09:41] Samir: rough ballpark: 0.5-2KB per active session for small prefixes, up to 50KB for large patient context. Console has a capacity planner that multiplies session counts, TTL, and average size to estimate GPU memory and node counts. We'll give you the export.
[10:12] Priya: what about multi-region — our data residency requires EU for EU patients.
[10:18] Jordan: routing by region is supported; you can pin model variants and cache to regions. For Private deployments, same console features apply, but network setup is customer-managed.
[10:31] Leah: we'll need a diagram for Private mode and on-prem KMS flow.
[10:36] Jordan: we'll include that in the package.
[10:45] [11:00] Samir: quick technical deep-dive note — when using quantized kernels for prefix cache, KV lookups are faster because memory bandwidth is lower; we saw ~15% token throughput improvement in tests.
[11:18] Marcus: how do we instrument for quality regression detection?
[11:22] Ana: Optimize integrates evals: you can pin prompt sets, run A/B with rollouts, and define quality thresholds tied to auto-rollback. We'll set up an initial eval with your top 50 prompts.
[11:40] Priya: that helps. any callouts re: vendor lock-in or proprietary formats?
[11:46] Samir: no vendor lock-in — models and tokens are standard; KV format is portable and there are export APIs. We also publish kernel compatibility notes for open-source runtimes.
[12:02] Jordan: ok wrapping — recap and next steps.
[12:08] Priya: thanks, useful; Marcus will coordinate benchmark infra.
[12:12] Jordan: next steps (readout): Jordan to share savings spreadsheet and recommended config (TTL 12h, batch target 6, prefetch lookahead 8). Samir to provide benchmark runbook and a 2-hour slot for a test. Marcus to share request histograms. Leah will gather compliance checklist for Private question.
[12:36] Samir: one more note — we recommend enabling a small canary of the quantized variant (5-10%) in week 1 once you have monitoring in place, to validate quality and cost.
[12:50] Priya: ok schedule that after benchmark.
[12:55] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the package and scheduling links.

Action items (as discussed): Jordan - send savings spreadsheet + config notes (by 2026-05-15); Samir - share benchmark runbook + suggested scripts (by 2026-05-18); Marcus - provide request distributions/logs (by 2026-05-17); Leah - list compliance questions for Private (by 2026-05-20).
